# Built-in workflows

<!-- Generated by scripts/dump_catalog.py from src/tin_lite/catalog.py. Do not edit. -->

Tin ships 39 built-in workflows. Every workflow also takes a `project_id`; required inputs are **bold**. An output of — means the workflow saves its results through its own executor rather than one declared artifact.

## Start here

| Workflow | What it does | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start here: onboard this business (agent only, human review)<br>`growth.onboarding` | Part 1: your agent fills the form from the codebase and the founder's two answers, and Tin writes the plan: the marketing systems ranked, what is usable in Tin, and what Tin would run for each. Part 2: the founder says in their words what Tin takes on and connects what it needs; Tin then sets those systems up as schedules and first runs and tells them what runs, what to expect and where to watch. | `product_url`, `system_hosting`, `system_repository`, `system_analytics`, `system_search_console`, `system_mailbox`, `system_payments`, `system_crm`, `system_support`, `system_docs`, `system_newsletter`, `system_ads`, `notes`, `priority`, `founder_hours`, `budget`, `urgency`, `outcome`, `timezone`, `hard_nos` | — |
| Start here: plan how Tin grows this business (agent only)<br>`growth.onboarding_plan` | From the product URL when there is one, the systems and notes your agent fills from the codebase, and the founder's multiple-choice constraints, read the site and any memory and write one plan: the marketing systems ranked for this business, which are usable in Tin today, a proposed scope, and what Tin would run system by system. Run inside Start here: onboard this business to have Tin set the picks up. | `product_url`, `system_hosting`, `system_repository`, `system_analytics`, `system_search_console`, `system_mailbox`, `system_payments`, `system_crm`, `system_support`, `system_docs`, `system_newsletter`, `system_ads`, `notes`, `priority`, `founder_hours`, `budget`, `urgency`, `outcome`, `timezone`, `hard_nos` | `reports/GROWTH_ONBOARDING_PLAN.md` |

## Organic traffic system

| Workflow | What it does | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run the organic traffic system<br>`organic.traffic_system` | Audit your website and research buyer searches, then save an editable content plan and draft its next article for review. With GitHub connected, adapt the approved article into an unmerged PR; otherwise keep its Markdown in Tin. Then draft the next planned article each week, one review at a time. Before new articles, refresh one existing page now and again each week. Optionally propose one technical fix. Never merges, publishes or sends outreach. | **`site_url`**, **`market`**, **`buyer_context`**, **`start_date`**, `duration`, `keyword_max_cost_usd`, `technical_fix`, `content_delivery`, `expected_repository`, `repository_serves_site`, `article_weekdays`, `article_local_time` | — |
| Prepare article PR<br>`content.deliver` | Adapt an approved article, answer page or public article to the connected website repository's own format, adding a Markdown route once when the site has none. Preserve its copy, open a reviewable GitHub PR, and keep the Markdown original in Tin. Tin merges the PR only when your delivery setting commits to main and the PR adds nothing but the page, or the page at the route you chose for such pages. | **`source_run_id`**, `retry_run_id`, **`expected_repository`**, `direction` | Unmerged GitHub PR, receipt `content/deliveries/{run_id}.md` |
| Change the website (agent only)<br>`website.change` | Put approved changes on your website repository: an approved article, answer page or public article, adapted to the site's own format at the route you chose with its copy unchanged; or the technical fixes the latest audit found, under site-fix-v5's rules, each a change you approve or decline once in Tin. A page you approved with commit to main, or fixes you approved, publish: Tin merges the pull request once your repository's required checks pass, then checks the live site. Anything else, and any change to a protected page such as /sign-in or one you added to the project's protected pages, opens a pull request for you to merge. | `source`, `source_run_id`, **`expected_repository`**, `repository_serves_site`, `finding_ids`, `decisions`, `protected_paths`, `retry_run_id`, `direction` | GitHub PR, merged when approved, receipt `website/changes/{run_id}.md` |
| Draft planned content (human review)<br>`content.generate` | Check current coverage before drafting the next planned article in your style. Save useful copy for review, or explain why no draft is needed. Optional GitHub PR delivery follows article approval. Nothing is merged or published and the roadmap stays unchanged. | **`program_id`**, `delivery`, `item_id`, `rewrite`, `plan_revision`, `direction` | `content/drafts/{run_id}.md` |
| Refresh an existing page (human review)<br>`content.refresh` | Pick the page from your latest audit with the most search impressions at stake: searchers see it near the top but rarely click, or it ranks just below the top results. Propose a new title, meta description and, where they miss the search, H1 and opening answer, in your positioning and voice. After you approve in Decisions, Tin changes exactly those lines in your site's source and follows your delivery setting. A page waits six weeks after a refresh goes live, and later runs report its clicks before and after. | `direction` | `content/refreshes/{run_folder}.md` |
| Capture writing style (human review)<br>`style.capture` | Use your coding agent to select writing samples, or add samples here. Review the proposed voice guide in Decisions; your coding agent can revise it first. Once you approve it, future content uses it. Nothing is published. | **`source_path`**, `direction` | — |
| Fix what the audit found<br>`organic.technical_fix` | Recheck an audit's findings on the live site and fix every one Tin can in one PR: indexing, the sitemap and robots.txt, redirects and merges, page structure, accessibility, structured data, social previews and internal links, in any framework. Your coding agent answers the judgment calls first. Copy stays with the content workflows, and steps outside the repository are listed. Tin checks each finding on the live site after you deploy. Never merges or deploys. | **`audit_run_id`**, **`audit_revision`**, `finding_ids`, `decisions`, **`expected_repository`**, **`repository_serves_site`**, `context` | Unmerged GitHub PR, receipt `reports/technical-fix/{run_id}/RESULT.md` |
| Plan upcoming content<br>`content.plan` | Turn an audit and keyword research into an editable two-week to six-month roadmap. Save to My system to prepare weekly batches. Does not write articles or publish. | **`audit_run_id`**, **`keyword_run_id`**, **`start_date`**, `duration`, `pieces_per_batch`, `context_files`, `amendment_id` | — |
| Plan keyword opportunities<br>`organic.keyword_plan` | Research buyer searches, competitor keywords, and a bounded sample of Google results. Get an evidence-backed keyword inventory for content planning. No audit or GitHub required; does not create a calendar, write articles, or publish. | **`site_url`**, **`market`**, **`buyer_context`**, `seed_phrases`, `competitor_hosts`, `audit_run_id`, `use_search_console`, `max_cost_usd` | — |
| Audit organic visibility<br>`organic.audit` | Audit technical SEO and AI visibility (GEO). Read robots.txt, sitemaps and Search Console queries, check up to 100 public pages by default, chosen by search impressions and URL section, and see whether AI answers mention, cite, or recommend your business, in the ChatGPT and Gemini apps, Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, and the Claude and Perplexity API models. Get prioritized findings with evidence and fixes. No GitHub required. | **`site_url`**, **`market`**, `refresh_questions` | — |
| Improve site health<br>`site.health_improve` | Retired: use Fix what the audit found, which repairs every finding of an organic audit in one pull request. Saved schedules of this workflow keep running: it inspects one public site against its GitHub repository, makes one bounded mechanical improvement and opens a pull request for review. | **`site_url`**, `focus`, `change_budget`, `context` | Unmerged GitHub PR, receipt `reports/site-health/{run_id}.md` |
| Audit AI visibility<br>`visibility.audit` | Retired: the organic audit measures AI visibility on the buyer prompt panel's questions. Saved schedules keep running: measure whether Luna finds and recommends a chosen target across five target-blind buyer questions, then publish AI_VISIBILITY.md. | **`target`** | — |
| Draft an answer page (human review)<br>`content.answer_page` | Create a public-facing Markdown content draft from the latest AI visibility findings; not for general advice or internal business questions. | — | — |
| Draft a public article (human review)<br>`content.public_article` | Turn durable project evidence and original thinking into a rigorous, reviewable public article. | **`brief`**, `audience`, `goal`, `length`, `source_policy`, `voice_notes` | `content/articles/{run_folder}.md` |

| Walk the signup as a new user<br>`qa.signup_walkthrough` | Sign up for your product as a stranger with a Tin-owned test account, verify the email, reach first activation, and report every break along the way. | **`product_url`**, `notes` | `reports/qa/signup/{host}/{started_at}.md` |

| Audit the product feature by feature<br>`qa.product_audit` | Exercise every feature in the project's Feature map as a user with a Tin-owned account and report what works, what is broken, and what to improve, with reproducible evidence. | **`product_url`**, `scope`, `depth`, `notes` | `reports/qa/audit/{host}/{started_at}.md` |

## Creative studio

| Workflow | What it does | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design a brand character (human review)<br>`creative.character` | Use when the founder has an explicit brand-design need. Design a vector mascot as an animatable SVG character in project Files (three mouth shapes, a blink, and a payoff expression), ready to narrate demo videos and appear in marketing. # Registry packages

26 contributed packages from `workflow_packages/` are selected in `src/tin_lite/public_workflows.py` and published with the next catalog sync. [The package guide](../workflow_packages/README.md#how-the-packages-fit-together) shows how they build on the built-ins.

## Organic traffic system

| Workflow | What it does | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan a sustainable social week (human review)<br>`social.content_plan` | Use current project context to make an editable social content plan with pillars, a weekly calendar, and a routine sized to available time. | `goal`, `hours_per_week`, `platforms`, `context_text` | `social/PLAN.md` |
| Draft social posts from a weekly plan or article (human review)<br>`social.post_batch` | Draft reviewable X and LinkedIn posts from an editable weekly plan and current source notes, or repurpose an article. Nothing is posted or scheduled. | `mode`, `plan_path`, `sources_path`, `raw_material`, `article_path`, `article_text` | `social/posts/{date}-{slug}.md` |
| Find the errors your users search for<br>`organic.error_surface` | Read the connected repository for the error messages your product shows users, check which your docs already answer, and get a ranked list of pages to write with the cause and fix from the code, ready to add to Plan upcoming content as a context file. It never writes pages, opens pull requests or estimates search volume. | `focus`, `depth`, `self_hosted`, `max_opportunities`, `docs_paths` | `reports/error-surface/{run_id}.md` |
| Turn unlinked mentions into backlink asks<br>`organic.mention_backlinks` | Each week, find pages and AI-cited sources that name your product without linking to your site, and get one short ask per page in your voice, never repeating an ask from an earlier week. It never sends, posts or contacts anyone. | `brand_name`, `domain`, `aliases`, `max_mentions`, `recency_days` | `reports/backlink-asks/{run_id}.md` |
| Take a weekly traffic snapshot and growth readout<br>`organic.traffic_snapshot` | Each week, read Search Console and PostHog once into one file. Per landing page it holds clicks, impressions and top searches, sessions by channel, first-touch signups and activation, reading depth and the latest audit's checks; Page decisions, the page tree and the blog index read it instead of querying again. The same file carries the weekly growth readout: where visitors and signups came from, by channel and by named AI assistant, search with a brand split, content and landing pages, with a change called only when an exact test with Holm's correction says it is real, and each decision naming the workflow that acts on it. No model calls; a failed read stays empty, never zero. | `signup_event`, `activation_event`, `activation_window_days`, `paid_event`, `website_hosts`, `brand_terms`, `exclude_email_domains`, `internal_flag_property`, `always_include`, `impressions_reliable_from`, `audit_run_id`, `content_paths`, `min_count`, `optional_rules`, `launch_dates` | `analytics/traffic-snapshot.json` |
| Decide what each page needs<br>`organic.content_efficacy` | Each week, judge every page the site shows in search from its clicks, visits, signups and audit findings: keep it, refresh it, rewrite it, merge it into a stronger page or retire it. Merges and retirements are held back whenever paid visits, links or a safe redirect target are unknown. Each URL change gets a stable ID for website.change, which asks you before it changes the site, and pages to refresh or rewrite are listed. Edits nothing itself. | `brand_terms`, `protected_paths`, `utility_paths`, `ad_paths`, `links_file`, `audit_run_id`, `max_rows` | `content/efficacy.md` |
| Plan the site's page tree and redirects<br>`organic.site_architecture` | Plan the site's page tree, URL and navigation rules from live data: the latest organic audit's summary (click depth, inbound links and checks for each page it crawled), a year of Search Console clicks, the traffic snapshot's visits and Page decisions. One model call names and groups the sections; code computes the rest. When URLs must change, it lists the exact redirects for website.change, which asks you about each one before it changes the site. Follow-ups after a change compare clicks with the saved baseline. It does not read the repository: click depth and possible orphans come from the pages the audit read. Plans only; changes nothing itself. | `mode`, `planned_change`, `new_paths`, `new_origin`, `applied_on`, `key_pages` | `reports/organic/site-architecture/SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md` |
| Build or fix the blog index<br>`content.blog_index` | Make every published article reachable within two clicks: trace where your connected repository keeps its posts, then open an unmerged PR for a blog index that lists them from that source, with dates, summaries, categories when there are enough posts, an RSS feed and sitemap dates taken from each post. Uses the route you chose for articles; if none is chosen yet, it asks you once instead. Reports each post's search clicks and impressions. Never merges or deploys. | `mode`, `page_size`, `featured` | Unmerged GitHub PR, receipt `reports/blog-index/{run_id}/RESULT.md` |
| Choose the buyer questions AI visibility is measured on<br>`organic.prompt_panel` | Write 36 buyer prompts in the words people type into an assistant: four intent families of eight, led by the category your product sells in, plus four that name your product. Code picks the families from your positioning and your own Search Console searches, leaving out searches for your name and comparison searches, and sets their weights; one model call writes the prompts, and code checks every rule before publishing. The organic audit asks the newest panel on its next run, so AI visibility is measured on the same questions every time. No review step: a panel that fails the checks is not published. | `target`, `seed_keywords`, `competitor_names` | `reports/research/prompt-panel/PROMPT_PANEL.md` |

## Cold outreach system

| Workflow | What it does | Inputs | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Find who pays and stays<br>`outreach.paying_segment` | A founder with Stripe subscriptions learns which customers keep paying, and gets exact inputs for the outreach shortlist, keyword plan and ads assessment to aim at them. Read-only; no model calls, and it starts nothing itself. | `retention_days`, `lookback_days`, `min_segment_size`, `exclude_domains`, `product_summary` | `reports/outreach/PAYING_SEGMENT.md` |
